product: Power and distribution transformers up to 800kV and 1500MVA, extra-high-voltage and gas-insulated switchgear, MV and LV circuit breakers, motors, generators, marine switchgear, battery energy storage, and GREENTRIC eco products including SF6-Free GIS and a 420kV SF6-free breaker.
demand: North American AI-datacenter buildout plus aged-grid replacement; US EHV transformer demand exceeds supply. Order backlog was USD8.49B in 2Q26, up 29.6% YoY, and the 2026 order target was raised 22.8% to USD5.185B on 2026-07-06. Reported US EHV market share number one for a second year.
pricing_power: Strong in EHV transformers where US shortage supports premium pricing and 2Q26 operating margin exceeded 25%. But the 2026-07-29 wave of broker target cuts on valuation and RoE, plus tariffs (2026-08-13) and industry capacity additions, signals concern that pricing and margin may be near a peak.
competition: Domestically Hyosung Heavy Industries and LS Electric; globally Hitachi Energy, Siemens Energy and GE Vernova. HD Hyundai Electric claims US EHV transformer share leadership for two straight years and 2026-08-27 US restrictions on Chinese grid equipment remove a low-cost rival. Competition is shifting to capacity and localization.
team: CEO Kim, Youngki, per the English IR page, pursuing US localization and eco-product strategy; workforce about 1998. Labor risk is real: the union entered dispute proceedings on 2026-08-04 over AI-era performance-sharing, and group-wide strike preparation was reported 2026-08-18.
market_strategy: Localize US production with Alabama plant one plus an expanding second plant, move from components into packaged power and distribution supply for datacenters, and push SF6-free eco products into Europe via the Paris grid expo, targeting a comprehensive energy-solution provider.
bull: 2Q26 revenue KRW1.1418T with operating profit KRW287.0B up 37.3% YoY and margin above 25%; backlog USD8.49B up 29.6%; 2026-07-02 Big Tech deal up to KRW1.1212T; US EHV share leader two years.
bear: 2Q26 EPS KRW5740 missed KRW6468 estimate; shares fell about 13% on 2026-07-29 as Nomura, Samsung, IBK and SK cut targets on valuation, RoE direction and new-business delays; labor strike vote 2026-08-18; KEPCO bid-rigging litigation 2026-09-18.
falsifier: 3Q26 earnings on 2026-10-22 showing operating margin below 25% or backlog below USD8.49B would prove the bull case wrong.

web_demand_price_volume_mix: Mainly demand and volume from North American AI-datacenter buildout plus grid replacement, with favorable mix toward high-margin extra-high-voltage transformers and distribution gear. 2Q26 revenue up about 26% YoY with operating margin above 25%. Order backlog USD8.49B at 2Q26, concentrated in North American hyperscaler and utility accounts.

Also global EHV incumbents Hitachi Energy, Siemens Energy and GE Vernova, and Korean peers Hyosung Heavy Industries and LS Electric, though all three ride the same boom.
web_contradicting_evidence: 2Q26 EPS KRW5740 missed the KRW6468 estimate and the stock fell about 13% on 2026-07-29 as Nomura (1.19M to 1.0M), Samsung (1.53M to 1.16M), IBK (1.5M to 1.2M) and SK cut targets on valuation, RoE direction and new-business delays. Shares are down about 24% in 63 days and roughly 50% below the KRW1430000 high. Labor dispute and strike vote (2026-08-04 and 2026-08-18). KEPCO bid-rigging litigation ongoing (2026-09-18).
web_if_management_right: Backlog near USD8.5B converts to revenue through 2027-28; 2026 revenue about KRW4.69T up 15% and EPS about KRW26607 up 31%. New US Alabama capacity (about USD200M second plant) plus 420kV SF6-free products open Europe. Consensus mean target KRW1171760 implies about 65% upside from KRW708000.
web_if_management_wrong: Backlog conversion and margin break first. If hyperscaler datacenter capex slows, or US tariffs and trade policy hit Korean exports, above-25% EHV margins compress and the enlarged Alabama investment under-utilises. Forward PE near 26.6x leaves little cushion; the KRW588727 low target (about minus 17%) marks the downside.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Electrical-steel and copper suppliers and transformer-oil or ester makers; Korean peers LS Electric (010120.KS) and Hyosung Heavy Industries (298040.KS). Within the group, HD Hyundai Heavy Industries (329180.KS) for datacenter engines and generators, and HD Hyundai Marine Solution. Grid EPC contractors and CJ OliveNetworks for smart-factory logistics.
